pr_title: Correctly protect DefaultChannelPipeline nodes when concurrent remova…
pr_body:
…ls happen due handlerAdded(...) throwing

Motivation:

We need to update the doubly-linked list nodes while holding a lock via synchronized in all cases as otherwise we may end-up with a corrupted pipeline. We missed this when calling remove0(...) due handlerAdded(...) throwing an exception.

Modifications:

- Correctly hold lock while update node
- Add assert
- Add unit test

Result:

Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/9528

issue_context.title: Handler is not really removed form the pipeline, although the handlerState is 'REMOVE_COMPLETE'
comments: @LightMingMing thanks for reporting... I think I know what is going on here which is very much unfortunate and may be very hard / expensive to fix for 4.1.x... This is fixed in master already.
@LightMingMing actually I was wrong... here is the fix https://github.com/netty/netty/pull/9530 .. Thanks again for the idea for the unit test.
@normanmaurer thanks for your reply, I took a look at your unit test, it's very graceful than mine...Thanks very much!

review_comments: Doesn't this imply that `remove0` should be `synchronized`?
@nitsanw it imply that `remove0` should only be called from a scope which is `synchronized(this)`
Isn't that exactly what a `synchronized` method does?
sure but why mark it `synchonized` when it is always called from a `synchronized` scope anyway ? If it is not called from a `synchronized` scope its a bug... Like here ;)

I understand this used to be a static method, and therefore you could not mark it as `synchronized`, but now that you can it would AFAICT prevent this bug far less verbosely (it would make the old code correct, make the assertion redundant). Is there a reason not to use `synchronized` here? :-)
@nitsanw I am not sure :) In many cases the synchronized need to not only have this code in but much more so I kind of preferred it to not have it on the method only and so make it more "verbose".
